feedback.problem: Find $(2a+5b)\cdot c+(b+3c)\cdot d,$ if $c\cdot a=2,$ $b\cdot c=3,$ $b\cdot d=4$ and $d\cdot c=1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Using the fact that the dot product is linear in the first variable, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(2a+5b)\cdot c+(b+3c)\cdot d & =(2a)\cdot c+(5b)\cdot c+b\cdot d+(3c)\cdot d \\  & =2(a\cdot c)+5(b\cdot c)+b\cdot d+3(c\cdot d).\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we can use the fact that the dot product is symmetric to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}2(a\cdot c)+5(b\cdot c)+b\cdot d+3(c\cdot d) & =2(c\cdot a)+5(b\cdot c)+b\cdot d+3(d\cdot c).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting the values for $c\cdot a,$ $b\cdot c,$ $b\cdot d,$ and $d\cdot c,$ we find

$$
\begin{aligned}2(c\cdot a)+5(b\cdot c)+b\cdot d+3(d\cdot c) & =2(2)+5(3)+4+3(1) \\  & =4+15+4+3 \\  & =26.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $(2a+5b)\cdot c+(b+3c)\cdot d=26.$
